TASK: The material handler was moving a pump casing from a floor pallet onto the maintenance bench. The task was underway because the casing was needed for a scheduled rebuild that morning. Stage of the task: transport, moving or handling material. Method in effect: SW-221 Manual Handling of Rotating Equipment. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method calls for the overhead hoist to be used for anything above 50 pounds, but the hoist was tagged out for inspection so the casing was lifted by hand. Equipment involved: Pump casing from unit P-118, and the maintenance bench in bay 3. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: Normal condition with no open maintenance items on either item. Object handled weighed approximately 95 pounds. Object size and shape: about 22 inches across and 14 inches deep, round with no hand holds. The object was held as follows: gripped underneath the flange with both hands, one handler at each side, wearing general purpose gloves. PPE in use: Safety glasses, steel toe boots and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: Immediately before the event: squatting at the near side of the pallet with the casing at floor level, feet apart and the second handler squatting opposite. At the moment of the event: the lift was called and both handlers raised the casing to about knee height, the far side was raised faster, the casing tilted toward the near handler, and the near handler twisted to the left to keep hold of it. Immediately after the event: the casing was lowered back onto the pallet, the near handler remained standing and reported pain across the lower back, and the lift was abandoned.

MECHANISM: Load or force involved: approximately 95 pounds shared between two handlers. The load moved from floor level to about knee height before the lift was abandoned. Body position during the movement: the load was held at about 20 inches in front of the body with the back bent forward, and the torso twisted to the left as the casing tilted. Assist device: The overhead hoist is the specified aid and was available in the bay but was tagged out for inspection that morning. This was a two-person lift. Coordination of the team lift: the lift was called by the far handler, the far side was raised roughly a second early, and the load tipped toward the near handler. Point of contact and direction of force: across the lower back on the left side, with the load pulling forward and to the left.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The hoist is normally used for this transfer and had been tagged out since the start of the shift. Conditions at the point of injury: congested or restricted working space. Detail: The bay was congested with parts staged for the rebuild, so the handlers could not stand square to the pallet. Timing: About 2 hours into an 8 hour shift and roughly 5 minutes into this task. The material handler had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: Risk assessment RA-118 covers manual handling of pump components and identifies loads above 50 pounds as requiring mechanical assistance. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The rebuild could have waited for the hoist inspection to finish, but the unit was needed back in service the same day.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: First aid at the scene: A cold pack was applied to the lower back in the first aid room for about 20 minutes. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notification: The supervisor was told within about two minutes and EHS within the hour. Scene and equipment: The station was left as it was and the area supervisor attended before work resumed. Work at the location stopped. The material handler was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
